how_it_works: Two-column split (roughly 40/60 on desktop). The LEFT column is position: sticky; top:0 (or top: ~15vh) and stays fixed inside the Work section while the RIGHT column scrolls the reverse-chronological experience entries. The left rail holds durable context: a section label ('EXPERIENCE'), and — the sharper variant of the Chiang pattern — an ACTIVE indicator that swaps as you scroll: the year range + role/org of whichever entry is currently in view (e.g. '2026 — PRESENT / Junior Clinical Data Scientist · nference'). Detection is via IntersectionObserver watching each right-column entry (rootMargin like '-45% 0px -45% 0px' so only the centered entry is 'active'); the observer sets active state that drives which year/role shows on the left. No page pin, no scroll-jack — native CSS sticky does the freezing, JS only toggles the active label. Nothing scrolls horizontally; scroll distance is exactly the natural height of the entries list. When the last entry leaves, the sticky rail un-sticks at the section's bottom (parent overflow bounds), so it never bleeds into Achievements. On the actual brittanychiang.com the sticky half also holds name/nav; the resume-Experience adaptation strips that down to just the section label + live year/role so it reads as a chapter header, not a nav.
visual_structure: A single beat = one experience entry in the right column: a mono year range as an overline (JetBrains Mono, muted, e.g. '2026 — PRESENT'), then role as the emphasis line (Inter/Fraunces medium), org on the same line or beneath, 1–3 tight bullets, and an optional proof chip row (skills/tech or a metric like '~90% test acc'). Beats stack vertically with generous whitespace and a hairline or left-border tick between them; they do NOT morph — they simply pass the sticky rail. The left rail is minimal: small-caps/mono section label pinned near the top, and below it the live 'year + role/org' that cross-fades as the active entry changes (the only moving text). Chiang's own version dims non-hovered rows and lifts the hovered/active one (subtle background card + translate) — the left rail is effectively the 'table of contents' that the right column indexes into. For Madhavi: lead/current role can be a slightly larger editorial beat, intern-under-FT shown as a continuity sub-beat within the same org rather than a duplicate card.
motion_recipe: Prefer CSS position: sticky for the rail (cheap, robust, no pin-spacer bugs) + IntersectionObserver for active-state — GSAP is optional here. If using GSAP to match the existing stack: do NOT pin the whole section; either keep CSS sticky and use ScrollTrigger.batch() only for the entry entrance stagger, or use ScrollTrigger with pin on the rail element (pin: '.rail', pinSpacing: false, end: 'bottom bottom') gated behind matchMedia('(min-width: 768px)'). Entries: fade + rise once (opacity 0→1, y 16→0, ease 'power2.out', ~0.5s, stagger ~0.08 via batch, toggleActions 'play none none none' — once, not scrub). Active label swap on the rail: quick 150–200ms opacity/blur cross-fade only (BlurText-style), driven by the observer, never scrubbed. DO NOT animate on scrub, do not pin the entire page, do not translate the rail continuously, do not animate layout/height of entries (jank + CLS). Test with markers:true; disable any pin on mobile (dynamic viewport height breaks pin math).
reduced_motion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, keep the layout but drop all motion. The left rail stays sticky (sticky is not motion — it's layout — and it still communicates chapter/context), but the active year/role swaps instantly (no cross-fade/blur). Entries render at their resting state (opacity 1, no y-offset, no stagger). Optionally, on very small screens or when reduced-motion is on, collapse to a single column: mono year overline directly above each role so the career path still reads top-to-bottom as a plain reverse-chronological list. No IntersectionObserver-driven emphasis is required for meaning — the year ranges alone carry the timeline.
brand_fit: HIGH. This is arguably the best-fit pattern for Madhavi's Experience block. It is editorial-minimal by nature (whitespace + typographic hierarchy, not effects), leans on the type system you already have (JetBrains Mono year ranges, Fraunces/Inter for role), and needs zero new dependencies — CSS sticky + IntersectionObserver, with optional GSAP for the entrance stagger only. It is the anti-slop choice: no purple SaaS glow, no scroll-jack, no horizontal scrub, no pinned full-screen takeover. It suits a dark-hero → light-paper (#FAF9F6) transition because the light Work area reads as a calm 'document' and the sticky maroon-accented label behaves like a running chapter head. Recruiter-friendly: reverse-chronological, skimmable, dates always visible on the left. One caution keeping it from being trivially HIGH: it is a very recognizable Chiang signature, so it must be re-skinned (paper not dark navy, maroon #8B2E2A accent not mint-green, serif display) so it reads as Madhavi's editorial system rather than a clone.
steal: Steal the LIVE left-rail indexing: keep 'EXPERIENCE' pinned at top of a sticky left column and, beneath it, a single line that cross-fades to the active entry's year + role/org as the right column scrolls (IntersectionObserver, centered rootMargin). It gives the whole block a spine and a sense of timeline/progress for near-zero cost and no scroll-jack — the mono year range on the left doubling as a quiet running timestamp is the highest-signal, lowest-effort detail to lift.
avoid: Avoid cloning Chiang's exact chrome and behavior: the dark-navy palette + mint accent, and especially the aggressive dimming of all non-active rows to low opacity. Recruiters skim — if inactive roles fade to ~0.4 opacity, they hurt scannability and read as a copied template. Also avoid pinning the full section (GSAP pin: true page-level) or adding smooth-scroll/scrub to the rail: it introduces CLS/pin-spacer bugs on mobile and scroll-jack friction for exactly the audience (recruiters) who want to move fast. Keep inactive entries fully legible; use the maroon accent only on the active tick, not a color wash.
